issues.description: The template Lecture.addGuestStudents method has a different parameter list than specified in the problem statement and implemented in the solution. The problem description and UML specify addGuestStudents(int): void, and the solution implements addGuestStudents(int). The template declares addGuestStudents(int, boolean), introducing an extra 'validateInput' parameter which will confuse students and prevent them from matching the expected signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the specification and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO */ }. If input validation is desired, either implement it internally in that method or provide an overload/helper method, but do not add an extra boolean parameter to the required signature.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify addGuestStudents(int) (single int parameter), and the solution implements public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). The template, however, declares public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) with an extra boolean parameter (validateInput). This mismatched method signature across artifacts creates a clear mapping confusion: students will follow the problem/UML expectation of a single-parameter method but the template's stub uses a different signature, which may prevent straightforward implementation or cause test/compilation mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's addGuestStudents method signature consistent with the problem/UML and solution by changing it to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). If input validation is desired, implement it inside that method or provide an additional overloaded private helper rather than changing the public signature expected by the exercise.
